item.title: Wrangling Two Monsters Part II: TDD with PICO C/C++ SDK in a Nutshell
item.description:
Intro

In part I, we’ve addressed the first monster, setting up a CMake project for TDD with Pico C/C++ SDK. This article will attempt to wrangle the second monster, the PICO C/C++ SDK itself

TDD Setup Overview

  • terms:

    • host build: code compiled for your development architecture (Your dev laptop)
    • target build: code compiled for the Pico board
    • target: generic reference for which platform the project is built
    • CMake target (for the purpose of this article): an item which will be produced by CMake build system
    • listfile: file containing CMake language

  • All development will be done in a Debian container

item.title: Wrangling Two Monsters Part I: CMake and Pico C/C++ SDK Setup for TDD
item.description:
Intro

Embedded world is a tedious place. The best way to navigate it while keeping your sanity is through the practice of Test Driven Development (TDD).

Being a bit blunt, Pico C/C++ SDK is a monstrosity (huge codebase with nested projects) managed by another monstrosity (CMake).

Nevertheless, both can be dealt with by using the popular strategy of “How to eat an elephant” - one small piece at a time.

item.title: Oh My: Maintainable = Testable + Understandable
item.description: So there you were… Palms sweaty, highly caffeinated, and ready to solve worlds problems with code. You have a brilliant idea that will solve this tough problem, however, it requires modifying existing code base. With plenty of creative freedom given by your boss, you embark on the journey of implementing this idea and bravely “improving” the existing code base. You’re finally done and and excited to see your great idea come to life.
